articles.headline: The One Thing About GTA 6's Ending to Know Before You Get Too Far In
keyFacts: Rockstar North co-head Rob Nelson said that Grand Theft Auto 6 features several possible endings with varying degrees of difference.
Nelson stated that the ending a player receives is determined by factors including story choices, the relationship system, criminal profiles, and family savings.
Nelson noted that there are no traditional good or bad endings in the game, and player choices naturally shape their specific conclusion.
body: While playing through Grand Theft Auto 6, you might notice that there are a lot of systems that can alter your experience. There’s the relationship system, your criminal profile, fitness routines that change your physique, and plenty more that gives you a lot of control over Jason and Lucia. In the moment-to-moment gameplay, it can be a little hard to figure out how much of that actually has an impact on the game.

Be warned, though: every choice you make really, really matters. GTA 6 features multiple endings that will be shaped by how much you engage with its systems. And it never makes it clear that those choices matter.
[Ed. note: This article contains spoilers for GTA 6’s ending.]

While I won’t reveal how my playthrough ended, I will note that I was faced with a binary choice that could have pushed me toward two different endings. GTA 6 has a few branching narrative moments like this where players are presented with two choices, so that lined up with the rest of the game. In my mind, I assumed that the game only had two endings. That was very incorrect.

That revelation came when Polygon spoke with Rockstar North co-head Rob Nelson ahead of GTA 6’s release. I had just rolled credits on the game, and Nelson was eager to learn which ending I got. I told him, and made a comment about the binary choice. He revealed that there were actually several possible endings with varying degrees of difference. Nelson said that some of them are small, maybe changing a bit of dialogue in a scene.

Others are more drastic. The climactic moment of my ending took place on a specific bridge on the map. Nelson said that some endings don’t go there at all. And while I’ve yet to see every ending play out (nor do I even know how many endings there are), I’ve already gotten the sense that the fates of certain characters can even change from ending to ending. If someone tries to spoil exactly what happens in GTA 6’s ending for you, know that you might end up getting surprised when something completely different occurs in your playthrough.

So, what determines which ending you get? Nelson told me that a few different factors go into it. The most obvious one is the choices that you make during branching story moments. You can also probably guess that the relationship system plays into it too. Your criminal profile is a factor as well, so even your choice of using lethal force in various situations can make a difference. On top of that, your ending can also change based on how much money you’ve stashed into your family savings account by the time you hit the credits. Needless to say, no decision goes without consequence in GTA 6.

If you’re stressing out about getting the “bad” ending by accident, don’t worry too much. Nelson noted that there aren’t exactly good or bad endings in GTA 6. Without spoiling where my story went, I can see where he’s coming from. The ending I got made perfect sense with the way I had been playing. And even within that moment, I still had a choice as to how it could play out. So long as you’re making deliberate choices in GTA 6 and not just ignoring systems for the heck of it, you should hopefully land on an ending that matches your playstyle. But keep all this in mind if you decide to ignore Jason and Lucia’s relationship. You’ll feel that eventually.

articles.headline: Fantasy Football Rankings: 5 most polarizing players for Week 11
keyFacts: Yahoo Sports analysts identified five polarizing players for Week 11 fantasy football using a coefficient of variation to measure ranking disagreements among their five rankers.

body: We have five Yahoo rankers every week , and this column will look at four of the buzziest names of the week. I'm looking for players where there is real disagreement, and I'm using a little something called "coefficient of variation" to help me find just that. These rankings will be tinkered all the way until kickoff, so please check back in on our weekly rankings pages and Sunday AM sit/start show for the absolute latest.

Colston Loveland (vs. NO) - 50.5 proj. yards

Loveland is the TE5 on TE3 usage since Week 6, when Caleb Williams returned. In his last 10 games together dating back to late in his rookie season, Loveland is averaging 11.4 half PPR points on 13.2 expected points, making him a fringe elite TE1. The true elites have disappeared with Brock Bowers healthy and the Cardinals projected for 12.5 points, so Loveland has a real case to take over as the short-term TE1 overall.

The Saints defense ranks sixth in half PPR points allowed to TEs at 13.1 per game, and they don't have the LB/S play to worry about. Harold Fannin Jr. had one of the best reps of the season against them in Week 9, and Isaiah Likely hung 99-1 on them over their last month of games. Chicago enters as 11.5-point home favorites with an implied team total of 30 points (fourth).
Patrick Mahomes (vs. ARI) - 20.4 proj. points

Mahomes exploded for 348 yards and five passing touchdowns against Atlanta in Week 10, bringing his season-long baseline up to QB6 (20.8 PPG). He has delivered +0.15 EPA per dropback (QB9) across his nine starts while chipping in 11.1 rushing yards per game (28th). I can make the case that the return of Rashee Rice and the addition of Josh Downs have the pass game in the best spot of the year right now.

Plus, the Cardinals defense can't stop anyone, allowing the third-most fantasy points to QBs this season. Matthew Stafford turned in three scores despite missing his top receivers last week, and Dak Prescott (QB11), Bo Nix (QB3) and Jared Goff (QB4) have all lit it up since September. It's not a surprise to see the Chiefs projected for 28.5 points (sixth). They won't have Kenneth Walker (groin), which could mean additional throwing production on the margins.
Bucky Irving (at DET) - 85.5 proj. total yards

This assumes Jalon Daniels is back at QB with Baker Mayfield (foot) picking up a new injury during the bye week. The Bucs are likely going to be extremely run-heavy, as they've been for the past two months with the OL smoking defenses up front. Irving has been the RB7 on RB11 usage this season, with 21.0+ half PPR points in 4 of 5 recent games. He's averaged 22.2 carries during that stretch, with games against pretty easy opponents. That's too big to fail, especially given how slippery he is on tape.

The Lions are a pass funnel typically, but the losses of LB Jack Campbell, EDGE Aidan Hutchinson and CB D.J. Reed (questionable) make them fairly bad in both phases. They still have some DTs to worry about, but the Bucs should be able to run it here, despite the spreadsheets suggesting otherwise. Tampa Bay will attempt to bleed out the clock as 7-point road dogs with a team total of 18.25 points (21st). Irving should absorb a lot of that team total.
Tetairoa McMillan (vs. BAL) - 63.5 proj. receiving yards

McMillan is averaging 8.2 half PPR points on 11.7 expected points in his eight games with Jalen Coker this year. Over the past month against a more difficult schedule, he's the WR53 on WR25 usage. He hasn't been getting as open of late, and then Bryce Young has missed him up the sideline a bit too often. He's still handling 24% of targets in an offense that leans pass-first in neutral situations, but the alpha WR1 traits haven't fully blossomed in his second season. He's a very good, not elite, WR to me.

The Ravens sent home podcaster Marlon Humphrey, not that he was very good in coverage this year. He'll battle with CB1 Nate Wiggins, who is much lighter but much faster than McMillan. There will be some 50/50 balls that he needs to come down with to win this individual matchup. Tre' Harris (WR24), Parker Washington (WR19), DJ Moore (WR13) and Tee Higgins (WR2) were able to do just that this past month against them. The Panthers are 2.5-point home favorites with an implied team total of 23.5 points (12th).
DeVonta Smith (vs. PIT) - 48.5 proj. receiving yards

Smith is expected to return after a pair of injuries have derailed his 2026 season. Since 2025, Smith is the WR21 on WR25 usage. While he doesn't have A.J. Brown to compete with, he also plays in a bottom-5 offense now. It's hard to calibrate all of the moving pieces, so Smith is a boom-bust WR3 until we have a better clue for how Joe Milton is going to fit in with Smith.
On top of that, the Steelers have an excellent DL that can spoil the entire game. Philly only has a 17.5-point team total, and I totally get it.

articles.headline: GTA 6’s Jason is nonchalant as hell, and the lead writer says it’s because of his 1970s heist movie inspiration
keyFacts: Rockstar Games senior vice president of narrative Rupert Humphries said Jason Duval's restrained nature was inspired by Steve McQueen in The Getaway and military research.
Game writer Michael Wiafe stated that the characters are based partly on research into decades of Florida criminal activity to create authentic, morally complex figures.
Game writer Elizabeth Gauvey-Kern expressed hope that players will share the protagonists' sense of determination and connect with both the high-stakes story and quiet moments.
body: Grand Theft Auto 6’s duo of protagonists are a team, but they really could not be more different from one another, despite their optional romance.

Throughout the little bits of in-game footage and marketing for GTA 6 we got over the years, it was clear that Jason Duval was reserved, soft-spoken, and nonchalant. It had a lot of people worried that he was too plain or bland. But according to Rupert Humphries, Rockstar Games’ senior vice president of narrative, the design of Jason’s restrained nature started with his heist movie inspirations, but also his military background.

Image via Rockstar Games “When we decided we wanted to tell a story about a couple on the run, we looked at all the similar kinds of movies, and one of the ones that really stood out was Peckinpah’s The Getaway ,” Humphries said over email in response to my inquiry about Jason’s general disposition. “Steve McQueen was famous for pulling lines out of scripts and saying things with his presence alone. We wanted to see how close we could get to that with a game character, where so many of our protagonists have been the opposite. This also resonated with the research we were doing around veterans and particularly former Army Rangers (in our world we call them Marauders). These guys typically aren’t running their mouths or reacting to something unless it’s strictly necessary, while still being strong and still asserting themselves.”

Jason does indeed remain this way in the final product: stoic throughout. But through the events of the plot, with exposition and backstory revelations in between missions, it’s subtly explained how and why he is the way he is, paired with the above narrative explanation. And I think it works perfectly as a foil to Lucia’s more spirited demeanor.

I haven’t seen The Getaway myself, but after watching a few clips, I can understand how Jason ended up this way. McQueen’s presence can carry a scene just with a glare or gesture, and Jason’s mannerisms echo this throughout the game while Lucia may handle things quite differently. But the character’s influences didn’t end there.

“Researching the prolific and headline-grabbing criminal activity that had been taking place over decades in Florida was an obvious starting point,” said game writer Michael Wiafe of GTA 6’s story. “From then on, it was about coming up with authentic characters that didn’t stray too far from reality but also were not totally bound by it either. The majority of our main characters are undeniably reprehensible on paper, full-blown criminals, but also decent human beings. Their moral makeup isn’t necessarily cut-and-dry, and we don’t attempt to make excuses for them. What’s important is how they resonate, no matter where you’re experiencing the game in the world.”
Make sure to check out our sister site, GTA 6 Bible for all your GTA 6 needs.

After experiencing GTA 6’s story in full, I can say that Jason and Lucia are two of the more relatable protagonists the franchise has ever had. They’re criminals who do bad things, but not necessarily horrible people (unless you play them that way), especially given their aspirations and situation that players find out about as they play. And it made me want to root for them even as they continued to wreak havoc across Leonida.

Image via Rockstar Games “The story takes some pretty heavy turns, but Jason and Lucia’s goal remains consistent,” said game writer Elizabeth Gauvey-Kern . “So sharing their sense of determination, the focus on their goal, through all the highs and lows — that’s what I hope people feel more than anything. You really want them to make it.”

“There were a lot of emotional beats to hit: On the one hand, you’ve got this saga through the madness of Leonida and all the highs and lows that come with that,” Gauvey-Kern continued. “But at the same time, you’re dealing with the quiet moments between this couple — the morning coffee, the long drives, the hanging out in bed. Those need to hit too, and you need to connect with how the characters are feeling in those moments.”

articles.headline: Can Jason And Lucia Actually Get Naked In Grand Theft Auto 6?
keyFacts: Players cannot make playable characters Jason and Lucia run around completely nude in Grand Theft Auto 6, despite earlier leaks suggesting otherwise.
Sex scenes and showering animations feature partial nudity, but the game restricts camera angles to prevent full frontal views of the main characters.
Other characters in the game appear fully nude in specific areas and missions, and PC players may gain full nudity options through future mods.
body: In the lead-up to Grand Theft Auto 6, there were leaks that showed the gameâs main boy toy Jason running around in the nude with his hog out. As such, many assumed this meant that players would be able to dress playable characters Jason and Lucia in their birthday suits as they went out and did crimes, adding public indecency to the growing list of legal wrongdoings the two are capable of committing. So now that the game is out, whatâs the truth? Well, you can see both characters naked, but the game doesnât show you everything.

There are a few ways Jason and Lucia show up in the nude throughout GTA6.Â As weâve already written about, the gameâs many sex scenes arenât porn-level explicit. Youâll definitely see a stray boob or butt cheek along the way, but you will not see any full frontal. You can shower and see whichever character youâre playing as from behind (Japanese players donât even get that!), but the camera angle is pretty set, and even swapping to photo mode wonât let you see whatâs going on up front.

Despite what was shown in the Cyberleek video, it doesnât seem like you can run around in the nude in GTA6. You can dress down to your skimpiest outfit, but there doesnât appear to be any way to go all-natural. Maybe that will change when the PC version comes out and modders get their hands on it.

While Jason and Lucia arenât baring it all, there is plenty of full frontal nudity throughout Grand Theft Auto 6. There are nudist areas, such as bars and beaches, where several NPCs are letting it all hang out, and there are even missions that will involve some pretty explicit imagery that we wonât spoil here, but if you donât mind such spoilers, you can read about one such example here. In any case, just know that if you donât leave any stones unturned, you will see some dicks and balls. Just not Jasonâs. PC modders will no doubt have a mission whenever GTA6 finally comes to the platform.

articles.headline: Meet the former Man United coach on brink of NWSL history with Kansas City Current
keyFacts: The Kansas City Current will face the Washington Spirit in the NWSL Championship on Saturday.
Head coach Chris Armas has led the Current to the final in his first season coaching professional women's soccer.
Armas previously served as an assistant coach at Manchester United under interim boss Ralf Rangnick.
body: The Kansas City Current are back in the NWSL Championship game for just the second time in the last nine years, seeking the city's first league title since 2015.
They will face Trinity Rodman and the Washington Spirit on Saturday, hoping to lift the NWSL trophy for the first time in the modern era of the club.
At the helm is a new face, not just to the Current but to sport in general, as Chris Armas looks to secure a league title in his first season coaching women's soccer professionally.

A former men's coach for his entire professional career, Armas has hit the ground running on the women's side, leading the Current to a fourth-placed finish in the NWSL regular season and knocking off the Shield winners Gotham FC in the semifinal to secure a place in the final.
Who is Kansas City Current head coach Chris Armas?
54-year-old Chris Armas is in his first year as head coach of the Kansas City Current, hired last offseason to take over the club.

It was his first professional women's soccer head coaching position, having previously spent his career as a head coach in Major League Soccer. Armas previously coached at the New York Red Bulls, Toronto FC, and the Colorado Rapids before moving over to the women's game.

Armas had a decorated career as a player, spending nearly his entire career with the Chicago Fire and winning the 1998 MLS Cup as well as the 2003 Supporters' Shield, plus four U.S. Open Cup titles. Armas also made 66 appearances for the U.S. national team, winning two CONCACAF Gold Cup titles.

The American has previously coached women's soccer back when he first began his coaching career at his alma mater Adelphi University, but moved to the men's side once he joined the Red Bulls staff in 2015.
When did Chris Armas coach at Manchester United?

A few months after being let go by Toronto FC in the summer of 2021, having managed the side for just 11 games before his dismissal, Chris Armas was hired by Manchester United as an assistant coach under interim boss Ralf Rangnick.
Armas had previously worked in the Red Bull system, as a longtime assist and then head coach of the New York Red Bulls, where he became familiar with Rangnick.

During his time at Old Trafford, the tabloids in England were not kind to the American assistant coach. According to a report by ESPN, Manchester United stars referred to Armas as "Ted Lasso" in a derogatory way, poking fun at him by comparing him to the bumbling but lovable TV character played by Jason Sudekis who had little knowledge of the game when he began coaching in the Premier League.

With Rangnick leaving the bulk of training to Armas, ESPN's report claimed that players felt the sessions were "old-fashioned," complaining that training was "often based on 11 vs. 11 work rather than dynamic drills they feel help to keep them sharp between games."

Despite the complaints, the performances on the field improved under Rangnick and Armas. Having fallen to eighth in the Premier League table by the start of December 2021, the team rose as high as fourth by mid-February, ultimately finishing sixth thanks to a lackluster finish to the campaign.
Armas left the club in May of 2022 after Rangnick departed and the club hired Erik ten Hag on a permanent basis.

articles.headline: Clarke: 'I am world class, I was just waiting for the world to see'
keyFacts: Cheavon Clarke secured a stoppage victory over former world champion Chris Billam-Smith.
Clarke stated to Sky Sports that he has always considered himself a world-class fighter.
Clarke expects Billam-Smith to take time to recover instead of immediately pursuing a rematch.
body: Cheavon Clarke: 'I've always been world class, I was just waiting for the world to catch up and see it'

"Chris Billam-Smith is a tough guy, and in boxing it's not the place to be tough." Cheavon Clarke reflects on his stunning victory over the former world champion; Watch Aaron McKenna vs Jevgenijs Aleksejevs on Friday December 4 live on Sky Sports
Friday 20 November 2026 12:25, UK
Cheavon Clarke catapulted himself into the top tier of the cruiserweight division with his stunning stoppage victory over Chris Billam-Smith.
Billam-Smith is a highly-experienced world champion, well known for hard-fought victories over the likes of Lawrence Okolie and Richard Riakporhe.
"I've always been world class. It's just waiting on the world to catch up and see it. That fight gave me the opportunity to do that. We're getting there," Clarke told Sky Sports.
When they fought at the Copper Box Arena earlier this month, Clarke did something no one had managed before - he dropped Billam-Smith (twice in fact) and stopped him.

"To Chris' detriment, he's a tough guy and in boxing it's not the place to be tough," Clarke said. "History is a great tell of the future. Every tough guy has a day where he's not tough no more. Unfortunately that was Chris' day."
Clarke has come back from defeat himself and doesn't rule out Billam-Smith doing the same.
"It doesn't mean that that's the end of it for Chris. Because he's been a world champion, he's got the experience, he can carry on," Clarke said.
"People need to stop writing him off. I've seen some comments online, just wild. It's not my business to be defending him, I'm not his lawyer… You just need to be factual."
Though he does expect Billam-Smith to take plenty of time to recover rather than pursue a rematch.
"There was talks of this after the fight, but who knows? What does it do for Chev's career right now, bearing in mind that I'm currently ranked above him," Clarke said.
"I'm looking to fight the guys above me and trying to make what makes sense for me."

articles.headline: 2026 CIAC high school boys soccer championship previews, top players, tickets and streaming
keyFacts: The 2026 CIAC high school boys soccer championship games are scheduled for Saturday and Sunday at Trinity Health Stadium in Hartford.
Tickets for the championship matches are digital only through GoFan, priced at $11.50 for adults, and games will stream on the NFHS Network.
The tournament features marquee matchups across classes LL, L, M, and S, highlighting undefeated teams, rematches, and programs breaking long championship droughts.
body: Berlin's Gavin Malec (11) celebrates his goal with teammate Berlin's Thomas Francalangia (28) during their CIAC Boys soccer semifinal game against New Milford Wednesday, November 18, 2026 at Municipal Stadium in Waterbury, Conn. (Jim Shannon/Hearst Connecticut Media)
Here is a closer look at the CIAC boys soccer championship games scheduled for Saturday, Nov. 15 and Sunday, Nov. 16 at Trinity Health Stadium, Hartford.
CLASS LL
No. 6 Greenwich vs. No. 1 Staples
WHEN: Sunday, Nov. 22, 12:30 p.m.
WHERE: Trinity Health Stadium, Hartford
SEEDS/RECORDS: No. 6 Greenwich (14-4-3) vs. No. 1 Staples (21-0-1)

TICKETS: GOFAN Adults $11.50, children 5 and under and military in uniform or with an I.D. are free. Digital tickets only (no cash sales at event) can be bought in advance. Screenshots of tickets will not be accepted.
ON THE AIR/WEB: NFHS Network (subscription required)
CHAMPIONSHIP GAME APPEARANCES

Greenwich is making its seventh championship game appearance and is 2-4 overall in finals. The Cardinals were the Class L champions in 2022 and were the runner-up last year. Staples is playing in the championship game for the 20th time and has won 13 championships. Staples is the defending Class LL champion.
KEY PLAYERS
Greenwich: Oliver Almeida, Sr., GK; Joe Carroll, Sr., F; Ebrima Touray, Sr., F.
Staples:
Thomas Pretty, Sr., D; Adrian Rodriguez, Sr., F; Noah Rossoni, Sr., M.
WHAT TO LOOK FOR

This is a rematch of last year's Class LL championship game , which Staples won 3-0 for its first state title since 2009. These two also met in last year's FCIAC championship, which Staples also won. When the two met during the regular season this year, Staples won 3-0 behind an Adrian Rodgriguez hat-trick.
YOU SHOULD KNOW

Staples is looking to remain undefeated in tournament play since head coach Liam Witham took over prior to the 2025 season. Staples has not lost a game this year, and Greenwich coach Kurt Putnam has stated plainly that Staples is clearly the best team in the state. There has not been a repeat champion in Class LL since Glastonbury did so in 2017 and 2018. Greenwich will try to erase a three-game losing streak against Staples to claim its second state title in five years.
CLASS L
No. 4 Berlin vs. No. 3 Bethel
WHEN: Sunday, Nov. 22, 5:30 p.m.
WHERE: Trinity Health Stadium, Hartford
SEEDS/RECORDS: No. 4 Berlin (14-6-1) vs. No. 3 Bethel (13-3-5)

TICKETS: GOFAN Adults $11.50, children 5 and under and military in uniform or with an I.D. are free. Digital tickets only (no cash sales at event) can be bought in advance. Screenshots of tickets will not be accepted.
ON THE AIR/WEB: NFHS Network (subscription required)
CHAMPIONSHIP GAME APPEARANCES

Bethel is appearing in its first CIAC championship game since 2010, and its seventh in program history. The Wildcats have had a remarkable track record in those six previous finals, never losing (with three shared titles). Berlin is making its first state championship game appearance.
KEY PLAYERS
Berlin:
Thomas Francalangia, Sr., F; Gavin Malec, Sr., F; Cole Pike, Sr., D
Bethel: Benjamin Garcia, So., D; Kevin Ly, Sr., F; Valentin Russo, Jr., M
WHAT TO LOOK FOR

Both of these teams have had to overcome difficulties to get here, and both are breaking long championship droughts. Bethel, which had been ranked a Top 10 seed in Class L every year since 2019, had not been able to get past the quarterfinal round in that time. Berlin has never gotten this far, a feat made even more impressive after its lackluster 1-4-1 start to the season. Both programs have been able to get it going at the right time.
YOU SHOULD KNOW

In the semifinal round, both Bethel and Berlin knocked out conference rival's of their championship opponent. Berlin defeated a New Milford team that had taken Bethel out in the SWC tournament semifinals. Bethel knocked off a Middletown team that split with Berlin in the regular season. Now the CCC vs. SWC story continues into a championship game that features two of the state's top goal scorers in Bethel's Kevin Ly and Berlin's Thomas Francalangia.
CLASS M
No. 2 Weston vs. No. 1 Waterford
WHEN: Saturday, Nov. 21, 3:30 p.m.
WHERE: Trinity Health Stadium, Hartford
SEEDS/RECORDS: No. 2 Weston (20-1-2) vs. No. 1 Waterford (19-1-1)

TICKETS: GOFAN Adults $11.50, children 5 and under and military in uniform or with an I.D. are free. Digital tickets only (no cash sales at event) can be bought in advance. Screenshots of tickets will not be accepted.
ON THE AIR/WEB: NFHS Network (subscription required)
CHAMPIONSHIP GAME APPEARANCES

Weston is making its fifth CIAC final in program history, and its second in three years. The Trojans lost to Tolland in 2024 and lost to Ellington in 2022. Weston is looking for its first title since 2005 when it was co-champions with East Catholic, its only CIAC title. Waterford, which has never won a CIAC title, is back in a championship game for the first time since 1987. This will be Waterford's third championship appearance.
KEY PLAYERS
Weston: Constantine Joannides, Sr., F; Mads Leary, Sr., M; Kyle Schiffer, Sr., D
Waterford: Mateus Fontoura-Oliveira, Jr., F; Bray Michonski, Sr., F; Jaydev Villa, Sr., M
WHAT TO LOOK FOR

Weston's defense, which is led by senior Kyle Schiffer and has only allowed 13 goals all season (including both the SWC tournament that it won for a second straight year and its previous CIAC playoff games), but will be tested against one of the most prolific goal scoring teams in the state. Waterford has scored 94 goals this season behind the trio of Jaydev Villa, Mateus Fontoura-Oliveira and Bray Michonski. The kicker here is that Waterford has also only allowed 13 goals this year.
YOU SHOULD KNOW

For the first time in three seasons, there will be a new Class M state champion. Weston knocked out two-time defending champion Tolland in the semifinals, opening the door for two programs that have never outright won a state championship game. Both teams have only lost one game this season, with Weston losing a regular season matchup against New Milford (which it avenged in the SWC championship game) and Waterford losing to Bacon Academy in penalties during the ECC semifinals.
CLASS S
No. 9 Valley Regional vs. No. 3 East Hampton
WHEN: Saturday, Nov. 21, 10 a.m.
WHERE: Trinity Health Stadium, Hartford
SEEDS/RECORDS: No. 9 Valley Regional (15-4-4) vs. No. 3 East Hampton (13-3-2)

TICKETS: GOFAN Adults $11.50, children 5 and under and military in uniform or with an I.D. are free. Digital tickets only (no cash sales at event) can be bought in advance. Screenshots of tickets will not be accepted.
ON THE AIR/WEB: NFHS Network (subscription required)
CHAMPIONSHIP GAME APPEARANCES

Valley Regional is making its 10th CIAC championship appearance and its first since 2010. Valley Regional last claimed a state title in 1997 when it split with Immaculate, and the program has a total of three championships. East Hampton is making its seventh finals appearance and its first since 2022, when it lost to Old Saybrook. East Hampton last claimed a title in 2014 when it split with Somers, but has lost in each of its other appearances.
KEY PLAYERS
Valley Regional: Aaron Johnson. Sr., D/M; Chris Kostek, Sr., D; Paul Malaguti, So., GK
East Hampton: Sean Hargreaves, Jr.; Grady Johnson, Jr., M; Sebastian Woodson, Sr., M
WHAT TO LOOK FOR

Valley Regional has been a team that has come alive in the postseason, reaching the Shoreline Conference championship game (which it lost to Morgan) before reaching the Class S final. Much of Valley Regional's success has been due to sophomore goalie Paul Malaguti and defenders Aaron Johnson and Chris Kostek, who have combined to not allow a goal in four CIAC tournament games. East Hampton has had a far more stressful path to the Class S final, despite a first round bye. It has gone to overtime twice in its three games, though Valley Regional did go to penalties in its semifinal victory over Stonington.
YOU SHOULD KNOW

This All-Shoreline championship will be the third time these two teams have met this season. Valley Regional defeated East Hampton 1-0 in the regular season, and Valley Regional was the victor again in penalties when the two met in the first round of the Shoreline Conference tournament

articles.headline: Fetterman ‘considering’ running for reelection as Democratic opposition to party rebel rises
keyFacts: Sen. John Fetterman said he is considering running for reelection in 2028 amid opposition within the Democratic Party.

Socialist Ahmed Moor launched a primary campaign against Fetterman, while several other Pennsylvania Democrats are weighing bids.
body: Sen. John Fetterman (D-PA) on Thursday said he is considering running for reelection, as the Pennsylvania lawmaker faces growing opposition within his own party.

Fetterman’s more centrist stance on Israel and immigration, among other issues, has increasingly thrust a divide between himself and the Democratic Party’s growing socialist and progressive wing, which particularly views the Middle Eastern democracy with deep distrust.

Though a number of Democrats have said they will challenge or are weighing a challenge to Fetterman for the party’s primary nomination in Pennsylvania, the incumbent senator has been silent on whether he will even run for reelection until this week.
“I am considering things, yeah,” Fetterman told reporters outside the U.S. Capitol when pressed on if he would run in 2028.
“I’m saying we are absorbing things and I’m fundraising and everything,” the senator added in remarks to CNN when asked about a 2028 bid.

When questioned on whether he is worried about primary challenges, the Democratic senator referenced former Rep. Conor Lamb (D-PA), whom Fetterman defeated in the Senate primary in 2022, and Rep. Brendan Boyle, who recently bowed out of a run against the incumbent lawmaker.
“Oh … ask Conor Lamb. What’s he doing?” Fetterman said.
“You have the little guy from Philly,” he said, referring to Boyle. “You can ask him why he chickened out.”

Socialist Ahmed Moor launched his campaign to oust Fetterman earlier this month. Reps. Chris Deluzio (D-PA) and Madeleine Dean (D-PA) are also weighing whether to challenge the senator in the Democratic primary. Reps. Summer Lee (D-PA) and Chrissy Houlahan (D-PA) are viewed as possible challengers, in addition to Lamb and State Rep. Malcolm Kenyatta.
JOSH SHAPIRO SIGNALS SUPPORT FOR ABOLISHING ELECTORAL COLLEGE

Moor, the first candidate to formally challenge Fetterman, has contrasted himself with the incumbent lawmaker by accusing Israel of committing genocide in its war against Hamas terrorists operating in Gaza, where the socialist candidate was born.

His campaign platform calls for “free healthcare,” abolishing Immigration and Customs Enforcement, overhauling housing and tax laws, ending the war in Iran , and targeting the White House’s tariffs. Moor has also demanded a moratorium on data centers in Pennsylvania.

articles.headline: Man Utd fan criticism has gone too far at times - Berrada
keyFacts: Manchester United chief executive Omar Berrada stated that while supporter frustration is understandable, some criticism of the club hierarchy has crossed a line.
Berrada defended the club's summer transfer business, stating that he is happy with the players brought in despite criticism over recruitment.
Head coach Mauricio Pochettino confirmed that Bruno Fernandes will remain captain for the upcoming match against Liverpool.
body: - Published
Manchester United chief executive Omar Berrada says some of the criticism aimed at the club's hierarchy has "crossed a line".

In a rare interview to Sky Sports as head coach Mauricio Pochettino prepares for his first game in charge, at Liverpool on Sunday, Berrada said he "understood" the frustration of supporters at United being 18th in the Premier League. He also said some of the criticism was "fair".
However, he feels some of it has gone too far.
"Being in this position comes naturally with the criticism and scrutiny we're going to get," he said. "We accept it. Some of it is fair, some of it does cross the line.

"We do live in this world of social media, where people like to generate negative stories about the club because it drives more engagement, and it drives more general noise and activity around the club. But we park that."
United's director of football Jason Wilcox has been singled out by supporters at recent games. There have also been social media calls for both Wilcox and Berrada to lose their jobs.

In addition, songs are now sung regularly calling for minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe to leave, while opposition to the Glazer family has remained intense since their leveraged buyout in 2005 saddled debt on to the club that now exceeds Â£1bn.
Man Utd happy with summer transfers; Pochettino wants say in future deals

Wilcox, in particular, has been blamed for what is perceived to have been poor summer recruitment. After the 2-0 defeat by Atletico Madrid in September, defender Lisandro Martinez said he "expected more from the technical director".

Ousted boss Michael Carrick felt he was let down by a transfer strategy that targeted midfield, while not addressing issues at left-back and in attack - which has been compounded by injuries to Luke Shaw and Benjamin Sesko.

Carrick wanted to target Elliot Anderson and Mateus Fernandes, but United backed off when Nottingham Forest and West Ham's demands went higher than they wanted to pay. Anderson eventually joined Manchester City for Â£116m, with Fernandes moving to Tottenham for Â£85m.

Instead, United paid a combined Â£118m for Carlos Baleba and Andrey Santos, who have started seven Premier League games between then, and triggered Youri Tielemans' Â£35m release clause at Aston Villa. Tielemans scored his first United goal in the 4-4 draw with Aston Villa on 8 November and has one assist.

However, Berrada has defended United's transfer business, saying: "When we look at the summer transfer window of 2026, I know we're receiving a lot of criticism for it, but we're actually happy with the players we bought.

"We think that Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos, and Karl Darlow - and let's not forget that we've also welcomed back Marcus Rashford, who had a very good season on loan at Barcelona - these are five additions that we think have made the squad fundamentally better.

"We went in knowing what we needed to do. Of course, there have been different dynamics at play and we've said consistently in the last few years we need to stay disciplined. We need to take the right decisions. We need to buy the right players, for the right value at the right time - in terms of what the squad needs.

"When we find the right opportunities, we will spend. But what we don't want to be doing is spending just for the sake of it. So, could we have signed an additional defender to straighten the depth and the quality? Yes, but we have to find the right players at the right value.
"There's no point in us spending Â£40m, Â£50m for players we're not convinced are going to add value to the team."

When he spoke to the wider media for the first time, 30 minutes before Berrada's interview was aired, Pochettino said he hoped to have a say in all areas of the playing side, even though his official title is head coach.
"I know that, being a head coach, I am the guy that is going to decide the squad for Sunday," he said. "I'm going to pick the starting 11 and I'm going to make the changes.
"Of course, in the future, I would like to be involved in all the main decisions that will happen on the squad."
We have to put Man Utd into a different place - Pochettino
Berrada said there had been little option other than to dismiss Carrick given United's plight and the team had "dropped off in many areas".
Pochettino has spoken individually to virtually every player to get an understanding of what the issues are.
He said he was wary of reading too much into data that shows United's players have not been running enough, arguing "if you don't put context on the data, it's very dangerous to talk".
The 54-year-old also said that, despite talking extensively about culture in his first in-house interview on Thursday, it could take 10 years to build one.
"The culture of the club and the identity of the club is very clear," he said. "It's a historic club, one of the best in the world. It's difficult to find another club the size of Manchester United.
"The culture of the club and the identity of the club is very clear. It needs to be in a different place than we are now."
Pochettino did confirm Bruno Fernandes will remain as skipper for the trip to Liverpool.
Fernandes has struggled for form and, with the 32-year-old's contract due to expire in the summer, there has been no breakthrough in negotiations over an extension.

United do have the option to trigger an additional year on the Portugal playmaker's present deal but, given the massive dip from the levels that earned him all last season's major player of the year awards, there are some who wonder whether a clean break might be best.
Pochettino preferred to deflect the wider aspect of Fernandes' future and concentrate on the immediate.
"Bruno is our captain and he's a very important player," he said.
"I think we will have time after to talk about the [other] things that you are asking me."

articles.headline: Russian missile hits Poland as Ukraine's allies hold military exercise, says Tusk
keyFacts: Poland said a Russian cruise missile and two other objects violated its airspace early on Friday.
Prime Minister Donald Tusk said the incident appeared non-accidental while Western military exercises took place in Poland.
Defence Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz said Poland would ask NATO for additional support following the incursions.
body: - Published

Poland says a Russian cruise missile was among three objects that violated its airspace early on Friday, with Prime Minister Donald Tusk saying it did not appear to be an accident when Western military exercises were taking place in the region.
Nobody was hurt and no damage has been reported, but Warsaw described the incident as a "provocation" from Moscow.
Russia has made no comment about the violations, which took place during one of its biggest aerial attacks on Ukraine since the start of the full-scale invasion in 2022.
Defence Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz said the Kh-101 missile hit a rural area at Nowy Lipowiec in southeastern Poland about 50km (31 miles) from the Ukrainian border.

The cruise missile, designed for precision targets, crashed at about 06:30 (5:30GMT) and Natalie Szponar, a local resident, said she was getting her children ready for school when she heard a "whistle and a dull impact".
The moment of impact was caught by a camera on a farm, and officials later made clear there was no risk to residents.
Another suspected missile went down near Rudnik nad Sanem to the west of Nowy Lipowiec, and a jet-powered drone crashed to the south near MoÅodycz, said Kosiniak-Kamysz.
He called the incursion into Polish airspace a "provocation" from Russia and said he would be asking Nato for additional support.

Nato Secretary General Mark Rutte condemned "grave violations of Polish airspace" and said Nato jets had been scrambled in response. "This incident is clearly dangerous - a consequence of Russia's ongoing war against Ukraine," said Rutte, who was due to visit Warsaw on Saturday.

A UK- and France-led exercise called Koalicja 2026 is currently taking place in southeastern Poland involving 11 countries that are part of the West's Coalition of the Willing group in preparation for a potential peace deal in Ukraine.

"It is no coincidence that these objects landed near the site where military manoeuvres by a 'coalition of the willing' supported by Polish troops are taking place in Nowa DÄba," Tusk told reporters on Friday.
Hours later, five coalition defence ministers - from the UK, France, Poland, Estonia and Lithuania - visited the military training ground where the drill was taking place.

UK Defence Secretary Wes Streeting told reporters that what had happened earlier was "yet another example of Russian provocation that is designed to divide Europe and to deter Ukraine's allies from supporting their fight for freedom and democracy".
In Brussels, UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the missile incident was "utterly unacceptable".
European Council President AntÃ³nio Costa expressed his "strong solidarity" with the Polish people and said Russia had to come to the negotiating table to bring the war to the end.

The violations of Polish airspace came a day after 40 countries took part in a Coalition of the Willing summit in Berlin, where the allies pledged continued support for Kyiv, and Chancellor Friedrich Merz said peace talks with Russia should take place soon on neutral territory.

At least eight people were killed on Friday as Russian missiles and drones targeted three of Kyiv's bridges across the River Dnipro and a station in Lviv, days after Russia's Vladimir Putin threatened "painful" retaliation for repeated strikes on Russia's bridge across the Kerch Strait to occupied Crimea.

This is not the first time the war in Ukraine has spilled over into Poland. In July a cruise missile also landed in Poland, leaving a 10m-wide (33ft) crater. That incident also took place during an attack on the western Ukrainian city of Lviv.

Casualties in Poland have been rare, while Ukraine suffers deadly attacks on a daily basis. However, two Polish farmers were killed by a missile in November 2022, which was believed to have been a Ukrainian air-defence missile responding to a Russian attack.
Moldovan officials said on Friday that their airspace had also been violated on Friday, when a drone crossed briefly into its territory during Russia's attacks on Ukraine.
The Moldovan defence ministry has recorded 118 such violations since the start of Russia's full-scale invasion in February 2022.

articles.headline: NYT report documents ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's decades of berating employees: 'He said he would rip both arms off a subordinate and beat the person over the head to death with them'
keyFacts: A New York Times report detailed allegations that former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang used humiliation, insults, and violent threats against employees for decades.

Despite the allegations, Huang retains significant support from employees, including a petition with over 200,000 signatures calling for his return.
body: It's been a strange couple of weeks for former Nvidia CEO, Jensen Huang. The once tech leader admitted to an affair, only for multiple affair allegations to surface, and he was then ousted from the company. Now, as he reportedly mounts a comeback, The New York Times has published a report detailing an alleged decades-long philosophy of getting more work out of employees "through humiliation".
Reportedly, Huang told employees that they had become so rich that "he couldn’t motivate them simply with money", so the "only way he could grind more work out of them was through humiliation".

This method has reportedly been Huang's modus operandi for some time, with more than a dozen current and former employees claiming: "He has long used humiliation as a tool, excoriating employees in front of their peers with insults, personal attacks and violent comments, while telling them it was good for them or for the business."

That humiliation allegedly took many forms. One employee reported that Huang "said he would rip both arms off a subordinate and beat the person over the head to death with them. And he told another employee he would rip off the top of their head and 'pee on your brain'."

Two years ago, in a conversation with Stripe's Patrick Collison, Jensen Huang said, "I'd rather torture you into greatness, because I believe in you", and this behaviour appears to be an extension of that philosophy.

Huang has apparently been called out for this behaviour. In the NYT report, Michael Winston, a former senior vice president of human resources, claims he threatened to sue Nvidia in 2005, after allegedly being fired for objecting to Huang's conduct. He says it is “the most verbally abusive, threatening and intimidating behavior” in his career and notes that Huang “thinks he can get away with anything.”
This lawsuit was apparently settled confidentially for more than $1 million, and was not previously public.

Still, Huang has quite a few supporters at Nvidia too. Reportedly, someone took to the Nvidia internal suggestion box before Huang's ousting to ask Nvidia to consider keeping him after the affair scandal, and this was met with 1,600 comments, the majority of which agreed with the claim. One said: "If you believe in the mission, bring back THE boss."

After this, a public petition titled "Bring Back Jensen" managed to achieve over 200,000 signatures. Huang's role at Nvidia can't be overstated, being the CEO since its founding in 1993. The gaming company turned AI company is worth trillions of dollars, and that no doubt means something to at least some employees who wouldn't be there without it.
Still, I can't say I'd be very happy if my editor told me they'd rip my arms off and beat me to death with them, regardless of how much money they're paying me.

James is a more recent PC gaming convert, often admiring graphics cards, cases, and motherboards from afar. It was not until 2019, after just finishing a degree in law and media, that they decided to throw out the last few years of education, build their PC, and start writing about gaming instead. In that time, he has covered the latest doodads, contraptions, and gismos, and loved every second of it. Hey, it’s better than writing case briefs.
